found_values.value: No finite longest stall with the console as written; 900 ms for one main-loop pass in which the USB host stops reading. The parts: (a) one flash window a pass, the longest a 4 kB sector erase, 400 ms maximum (packaged-part figure, W25Q16JV-DTR revision I tSE; the die's figure is not known); out_store_tick() runs once a pass and out_store_reclaim() only on a pass where the tick did nothing (main.c:1049, :1083). (b) each console write: pico-sdk 2.3.0 stdio_usb_out_chars() leaves its loop early only when no space is free and more than PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed since the last accepted chunk (stdio_usb.c:122); the default is 500,000 us (stdio_usb.h:31-33) and the tree does not override it. (c) 400 ms erase plus one 500 ms blocked printf (main.c:1059-1067): 900 ms. (d) no bound but the message length while the host keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written, because each accepted chunk restarts the 500 ms. (e) at boot, up to 2 sector erases before CAN starts (main.c:923-939): 800 ms plus prints, counted only if the watchdog runs by then. On the IO board Q8 moves the output binding to an I2C FRAM (owner, 2026-09-29), which takes the erase out of the loop once the firmware follows it (hardware/STATUS.md:76); the firmware in this checkout still erases flash

found_values.value: 1000 ppm total: tolerance at 25 C, stability over the operating range and first-year ageing together. Section 8.1.2.3: 'the design to tolerate up to 1000ppm variation in the XOSC frequency'; section 8.6: the PLLs drive clocks at their maximum 'as long as the reference clock is accurate to 1000ppm'. Looser limits: USB full speed 12.000 Mb/s +/-0.25 % (2,500 ppm, USB 2.0 section 7.1.11); the bidirectional DShot decoder, host-tested at +/-5 % (docs/DShot.md:221-230), against an ESC at +/-2 % (V3), leaves 3 %. The CAN controllers take their own 40 MHz clock (owner, 2026-10-01, IOBoard.md:141), so the CAN bit rate does not depend on this crystal

found_values.value: Load capacitance 10 pF; ESR at most 50 Ohm; drive-level rating at least 200 uW. Table 597 gives the crystal the XOSC is specified with, the ABM8-272-T3: CL 10 pF, ESR (R1) 50 Ohm max, drive level 10 uW typical and 200 uW max. Hardware design with RP2350, section 4: a maximum ESR of 50 Ohm 'along with a 1 kOhm series resistor (R2), is a good value to prevent the crystal being over-driven'; two 15 pF capacitors plus parasitics give '10.5pF, which is close enough to the target of 10 pF'. Neither document states the drive level the circuit applies; the 200 uW rating of the specified crystal is taken as the lowest rating a crystal may have
found_values.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29 (SHA-256 2877d0f2...4be8), https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf, section 8.2.1.1, Table 597; Hardware design with RP2350, build date 20/08/2026 (SHA-256 cef88bc7d87e67b4262ee15f2b94b03566667143f4e8daf6931828bef6408059), https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/hardware-design-with-rp2350.pdf, section 4 (text lines 547-562)

found_values.value: At most 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground on each of D+ and D-, shared by the RP2354B's USB pin, the connector and the protection, with D+ and D- differing by less than 10 %. USB 2.0 section 7.1.6.1: an upstream-facing full-speed port with a detachable cable may have 100 pF (CINUB), 'comprised of up to 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground on each line at the transceiver and in the connector and an additional 25 pF capacitance on each conductor in the transmission line'; 'The difference in capacitance between D+ and D- must be less than 10%'. The RP2350 datasheet gives no capacitance for USB_DP and USB_DM (Table 1437), so the share left for the protection is not known
found_values.source: USB 2.0 specification usb_20.pdf (SHA-256 d39698a33486c399124af92bd02e4f978fd9a836b5cf4e52e6e4633eb1d89f61) in https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/usb_20_20250603.zip, section 7.1.6.1, read 2026-10-01T21:38:50Z; RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29 (SHA-256 2877d0f2...4be8), Table 1437, read 2026-10-01T21:33:09Z

report.value: 13 errata affect stepping A4: E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8, E11, E12, E17, E26, E27, E28. report.value: The RP2350 watchdog counts down in microseconds from LOAD (24 bits, up to 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds', Table 1249), is disabled at reset (CTRL.ENABLE 0x0) and pauses in debug (PAUSE_DBG0/1, PAUSE_JTAG reset 1, Table 1248). Against the stop deadline (V1, 500 ms): the part can set any timeout under 500 ms; the time from expiry to the pads at their reset state is not stated. Against the longest legitimate stall (V2 as found): 900 ms for a pass with a 400 ms packaged-part sector erase and one 500 ms blocked console write, and no bound with a host that keeps accepting slowly, since each accepted chunk restarts pico-sdk's 500,000 us PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US, which the tree does not override. So no timeout meets both while the firmware erases flash in the loop and the console write is uncapped. A window opens once the store moves to the FRAM (Q8) and the console write is capped below 500 ms less the rest of the pass and the reset; the cap is not stated (hardware/STATUS.md:76). The image sets no timeout (V4). For the owner: the console-write cap and the timeout, in firmware. Not a defect of the part

found_values.value: At most 9 frames in a 400 ms stall and at most 8 in a 3 ms stall. Outside the start-up self-test the panel keeps one request outstanding (start() refuses a request while one is pending) until its answer or its own 1000 ms timeout, so a stall under 1000 ms sees one request's frames at most: 8, a 32-register write at 4 registers a frame. During the 1200 ms start-up self-test the panel sends one status request or one probe at a time, the next once the last is 50 ms old and unanswered; the IO board's controller still acknowledges in hardware during a stall, so nothing is retransmitted. 400 ms then holds at most 9 frames 50 ms apart (10 would need more than 400 ms); 3 ms holds 1 self-test frame, or 8 from one write. Unchanged from FU-A2's finding; re-read at checkout 08042b06b2dc.

found_values.value: At most 11,495 frames in 400 ms and at most 87 in 3 ms: the bound of a saturated bus at V20's CAN FD with V21's 1000/5000 kbit/s; the tree defines no traffic on the port. Shortest frame counted: a CAN FD base-format frame with no data and bit-rate switching, 16 bits (SOF, 11 identifier bits, RRS, IDE, FDF, res) and 12 bits (ACK slot, ACK delimiter, 7 EOF, 3 intermission) at 1000 kbit/s = 28 us, plus 34 bits (BRS, ESI, 4 DLC, 4-bit stuff count, 17-bit CRC, 6 fixed stuff bits, CRC delimiter) at 5000 kbit/s = 6.8 us: 34.8 us, a lower bound (dynamic stuff bits left out). 400,000/34.8 = 11,494.3 and 3,000/34.8 = 86.2, each plus one for a frame ending inside the window. A longer stuff-count field than 4 bits only lengthens the frame and keeps the bound. ISO 11898-1 not read.

found_values.value: DS20006027B states for the 40 MHz clock: '40, 20 or 4 MHz Crystal or Ceramic Resonator; External Clock Input' (page 1, section 5.0); FOSC1,40M 40 MHz -0.5 % to +0.5 % for a crystal or resonator; GM,40M transconductance 2040 to 3060 uA/V (design guidance); TOSCSTAB 3 ms from POR; external digital clock FOSC1,CLKI 2 to 40 MHz with no tolerance, duty cycle 45 to 55 %, OSC1 high and low time 0.45 to 0.55 TOSC, rise and fall 20 ns max (Table 7-3); OSC1 VIH 0.7 VDD to VDD + 0.3 V, VIL -0.3 V to 0.3 VDD, VOSCPP 0.5 V peak-to-peak minimum, ILI +/-5 uA (Table 7-1). Not stated in the datasheet: the crystal's load capacitance, highest ESR, drive level, shunt capacitance C0, cut and mode; the OSC1 and OSC2 pin capacitance; what OSC2 does with an external clock; and an oscillator's supply current limit. P2 applies a derived crystal limit: gain margin gm/gmcrit >= 5 with gm at its 2040 uA/V minimum and gmcrit = 4 x ESR x (2 pi F)^2 x (C0 + CL)^2 (ST AN2867), which at 40 MHz is ESR x (C0 + CL)^2 <= 1.615e-21 Ohm F^2, for example ESR <= 25 Ohm at C0 + CL = 8 pF; fundamental mode, since the datasheet names no overtone network. The MCP251863 datasheet (DS20006624B Table 9-4) gives the same figures.

report.value: Section 8.2.2 step 5b: VCC not connected, 'can tolerate higher signal swing in the range up to 10 V', a 0.1 uF still at VCC. missed.why: P2 considered only the SG-8101CB of this family (C390561). The SG-8101CE is the same Epson programmable CMOS oscillator in the 3.2 x 2.5 mm package. Figures from the Epson data sheet for SG-8101CG/CE/CB/CA, Spec No SG-8101series_E_Ver2.0 (https://download.epsondevice.com/td/pdf/app/SG-8101CE_en.pdf, read 2026-10-01T22:14:37Z): frequency tolerance +/-15 ppm at -40 to +85 degC including aging (limit 3,876 ppm); VCC 1.62 to 3.63 V, so the 3.3 V rail 3.201 to 3.399 V is inside; CMOS output, symmetry 45 to 55 % at 50 % VCC with a load of 15 pF or less (OSC1 asks 45 to 55 %); rise and fall time 6 ns max at 20 to 80 % for grade A at fo up to 40 MHz (OSC1 asks 20 ns); VOH at least 90 % VCC at -3.0 mA and VOL at most 10 % VCC at VCC 2.70 to 3.63 V (OSC1 asks 0.7 VDD high, 0.3 VDD low); ICC 4.4 mA max at 20 to 50 MHz, VCC 2.70 to 3.63 V, no load; start-up 3 ms max; ordering code T (1.8 to 3.3 V), BG (+/-15 ppm, -40 to +85 degC), P (output enable on pin 1), A (default edge). Pin 1 is OE and the data sheet says not to use it open, so it is tied to the 3.3 V rail. Pads: #1 OE, #2 GND, #3 OUT, #4 VCC. JLCPCB C390554 (vendors.py jlcpcb, 2026-10-01T22:10:33Z): stockCount 853, canPresaleNumber 847, library 'expand', 0.7023 USD at 10, description '-40 to +85 degC 1.8V~3.3V 40MHz +/-15ppm SMD3225-4P'. Digi-Key keyword search 'SG-8101CE 40.0000M' (2026-10-01T22:09:57Z): SG-8101CE 40.0000M-TBGPA0 Active, stock 0, manufacturer lead 6 weeks; so its second source under rule 5 is a pin-compatible alternate, and X1G0059610009 (C7504304, SG3225CAN, same 3225-4P footprint, pads #1 ST, #2 GND, #3 OUT, #4 VCC per SGxxxxCAN_E_Ver3.0, https://download.epsondevice.com/td/pdf/app/SG3225CAN_en.pdf, read 2026-10-01T22:10:12Z) is that alternate: JLCPCB 91, presale 91 (22:10:33Z), over the gate of 50 for 2 placements x 5 boards. Epson's product page https://www.epsondevice.com/crystal/en/products/crystal-oscillator/sg8101ce.html (22:10:33Z) states no lifecycle status; Digi-Key's status for the 40 MHz variants is Active. Market introduction date not read. On P2's own order (an oscillator above a crystal; JLCPCB stock well over the gate) the pair C390554 with C7504304 sits above rank 3, the ABM8W crystal (JLCPCB 73, 4 pF load, drive level not shown). The pair has a stated data-sheet grade and a second source; rank 2's product number is not in Epson's standard table.

exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: Meets every value but ranks below the three: JLCPCB 91; the Digi-Key keyword search 'SG3225CAN 40.000000M-TJGA3' returned no product, so no second source is shown.
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: Rule 5 accepts a pin-compatible alternate that passes rules 1 to 4 as the second source, not only the same part at Digi-Key. SG-8101CE 40.000000MHz TBGPA (C390554) is such an alternate: same 3.2 x 2.5 mm 4-pad package and pad functions (#1 ST or OE, #2 GND, #3 OUT, #4 VCC), CMOS, 1.62 to 3.63 V, 45 to 55 % symmetry, Epson (S2), JLCPCB stockCount 853, presale 847 at 2026-10-01T22:10:33Z, against the gate of 50. Pin 1 tied to the 3.3 V rail suits both parts (the SG-8101 data sheet forbids pin 1 open; the SG3225CAN allows high or open). C7504304 itself reads JLCPCB 91, presale 91 at the same time, so the pair passes rule 4 and rule 5 together, and the drop reason 'no second source shown' does not hold. Frequency tolerance of the SG3225CAN at -40 to +85 degC is +/-25 ppm (SGxxxxCAN_E_Ver3.0 section 4), inside 3,876 ppm. Sources: https://download.epsondevice.com/td/pdf/app/SG3225CAN_en.pdf (22:10:12Z); https://download.epsondevice.com/td/pdf/app/SG-8101CE_en.pdf (22:14:37Z).

data.ruling:
The refutation does not hold. The RP2354B stays for "Microcontroller". The stock verifier confirms the part and refutes nothing: its refutation text is empty and all 14 of its checks pass. The datasheet verifier fails 3 checks: watchdog stall cover (V2), watchdog window (V1 and V2), and image watchdog timeout (V4). The verifier itself says each one fails on the firmware, not on the part. I re-read the sources and agree.

(1) What the part can do. RP2350 datasheet Table 1249 (LOAD, bits 23:0) allows any timeout up to 0xffffff us, which is 16,777,215 us or about 16.8 s. CTRL.ENABLE resets to 0 (Table 1248), so firmware turns the watchdog on. Any timeout under V1's 500 ms can be set. So can any timeout above the 400 ms packaged-part maximum for a W25Q16JV sector erase. The window between 400 ms and 500 ms, less the reset time, exists on this part. The datasheet does not state the time from expiry to the pads reaching their reset state. That time is not read.

(2) V2, the stall. The 900 ms figure is one 400 ms erase followed by a console write in the same main-loop pass (main.c:1049-1089). With a slow host the stall has no bound. In pico-sdk 2.3.0, stdio_usb_out_chars() sets last_avail_time after every chunk the host accepts (stdio_usb.c:118). It gives up only after PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US with nothing accepted (stdio_usb.c:122). That constant is 500,000 us by default, and the build can override it (stdio_usb.h:31-33). Both the erase in the loop and the console write are firmware choices. The firmware can move the store: Q8 is decided, and the output binding moves to the MB85RC256VPNF-G-AMERE2 FRAM (owner, 2026-09-29). It can also cap the console write. No microcontroller's watchdog can cover a stall with no bound. The part does not cause that stall.

(3) V4, the timeout the image sets. Searching firmware/iomcu/ for "watchdog" finds only the comment at main.c:970-973, with no watchdog_enable() or watchdog_update(). So the image sets no timeout. That is the value found for V4. It is a gap in the firmware, not a datasheet value. The specification already records it: IOBoard.md:251 says "The image enables none". hardware/STATUS.md:76 lists the timeout, the console-write cap and the move of the store to the FRAM as firmware work.

This is the third time the same question has come up. FU-A4 adjudicator-R1 (007) ruled the same way on the same three watchdog checks: not a property of the part.

The RP2354B is also a fixed input. Under Research.md Scope, a fixed input is checked for stock, lifecycle and a second source. One that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. The watchdog findings go to the owner and to firmware as findings: there is no timeout in the image, and the console-write cap is not stated.

Part-level facts I re-read all pass:
- JLCPCB C39843328 is RP2354B, Raspberry Pi, QFN-80-EP(10x10), erpComponentName SC1512(13)-A4. stockCount is 2535, which passes the gate of 50 (max(5 x 10, 50)). canPresaleNumber is 2418.
- The Raspberry Pi PCN (product change notice) listing still holds only "RP235x A4 stepping PCN". That notice ends the steppings other than A4. It is not an end-of-life notice for the A4 part.
- 20 held parts cover the need of 10: 5 boards x 2 a board.
- Raspberry Pi is on the S1 allowlist.

found_values.value: set: the latch powers up holding the gates disabled, and only the operator clear control enables them after power-up; the latch reset input is tied to the enable node, which stays low through the 3.3 V ramp
found_values.source: STATUS.md@08042b0:340 ('Every stop latches; nothing re-arms on its own.'); F11 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:672; IOBoard.md@08042b0:224 and :226

found_values.value: between the enable node and the gates: the latch output drives the output buffer enable, the servo rail gate drivers, both ESC pack switch drivers and the external CAN transceiver standby; the enable node keeps the monostable's own timing, which test steps 7 and 10 read
found_values.source: Monostable.md@23c82ca:557-561 (step 7) and :582-585 (step 10); IOBoard.md@08042b0:226

found_values.value: a momentary normally-open push button on the IO board, wired to the latch clock through a resistor-capacitor debounce and a Schmitt buffer (SN74AUP1G17DBVR), with no processor, register or firmware between contact and latch
found_values.source: F11 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:672; Monostable.md@23c82ca:449-455; IOBoard.md@08042b0:227 and :244

found_values.value: relay: no; firmware on either board: no. F11 asks a clear 'only by an operator action', and no processor, register or firmware sits in the path from GPIO6 to either gate
found_values.source: F11 question and Answer, Research.md@08042b0:672; Monostable.md@23c82ca:449-455; IOBoard.md@08042b0:227

found_values.value: yes: the high-side switch on each servo rail is the servo rail gate, one on each of the 3 servo rails and one on the adjustable supply output; the 20 port supply switches, driven through the I/O expander, are not a gate
found_values.source: IOBoard.md@08042b0:218 and :248 (owner, 2026-09-30); Monostable.md@23c82ca:449-455

found_values.value: at least 17.8 V above 67.2 V, so a rating of at least 85 V: the open switch holds the pack node up to the clamp level, which stays under the INA228 85 V; a 100 V part (32.8 V margin) meets it, an 80 V part (12.8 V) does not
found_values.source: [D1], section 6.1 (VCM and VVBUS -0.3 V to 85 V); F15 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:676; Power.md, motor monitor INA228 (owner, 2026-09-30)

found_values.value: 300 A: the owner's V50 answer, a peak of 300 A for 30 s at most; 'and more' carries no figure
found_values.source: V50 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:747

found_values.value: from the 74HC423 datasheet only the supply term: Fig. 7 (typical K at 25 degC, external capacitance 10 nF, 10 kOhm to 100 kOhm) digitized at 600 dpi gives K 0.4810 at 3.201 V, 0.4780 at 3.3 V and 0.4750 at 3.399 V, +0.63 % / -0.63 %; the datasheet neither graphs nor limits K against temperature, so the temperature term is not read
found_values.source: [D2], Fig. 7 (page 9 rendered at 600 dpi on its gridlines)

found_values.value: 0.57 uA at 50 degC for the 74HC423: its input leakage limit of +/-0.1 uA at 25 degC (VCC 6.0 V) doubled every 10 degC (0.1 x 2^2.5 = 0.566 uA); the table limits the same leakage to +/-1.0 uA over -40 to 85 degC and gives no separate figure for the nREXT/CEXT pin
found_values.source: [D2], Table 6 (II)

found_values.value: 0 to 50 degC ambient: the owner answers V38 through V270 (2026-10-01)
found_values.source: V270 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:967

found_values.value: under 5 mA a rail: the placeholder of pull request #167 is the idle current of the lightest load; a micro servo, Savox SH-0255MG+, states a quiescent current of 5 mA
found_values.source: Monostable.md@23c82ca:411-416; Savox SH-0255MG+ product page, 'Quiescent Current (mA) 5', [D3]

found_values.value: none: only switching transients are clamped; the highest sustained input is the 67.2 V of a 16-cell pack at 4.2 V a cell
found_values.source: F15 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:676; V41 question, Research.md@08042b0:738

found_values.value: 125 ns: the 74HC423 nRD LOW pulse width minimum over -40 to 85 degC at VCC 2.0 V, the lowest supply its table gives; the term the 3.3 V regulator ramp sets is the P5 power-up check against the regulator R5 selects
found_values.source: [D2], Table 7 (nRD input LOW pulse width)

found_values.value: at least 20 V: the TPS55285 programs its output from 0.8 V to 15 V, its output overvoltage protection trips at 110.5 % to 120 % of the set point (18 V at 15 V), its VOUT pin is rated to 17 V absolute maximum, and the board DC input reaching it is 20 V at most
found_values.source: [D4], sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 (VOUT, VVOUT_OVP_FB); DC input row, IOBoard.md@08042b0:355

found_values.value: yes: an ESC with regenerative braking returns current to the pack through the closed switch; the tree states no figure for that current, so the onboard path 150 A continuous rating (F2) bounds it in either direction
found_values.source: shared/ui/programmer_screen.c@08042b0:199-201 ('Regen braking ... Puts braking energy back into the pack'); F2 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:663

found_values.value: 2.8 V: SET_PACK_CELLS takes 1 cell, and the lowest per-cell low-voltage cut the tree offers for an ESC is 2.8 V, so a 1-cell ESC pack can run down to 2.8 V
found_values.source: shared/settings/settings.c@08042b0:39-41 (pack_cells 1 to 14); shared/ui/programmer_screen.c@08042b0:139-141 and :202-204 ('Low voltage cut', 28 to 38 tenths of a volt)

found_values.value: level: the latch sets on the enable node's low level (the enable node drives the latch reset), and set wins when set and clear are both active
found_values.source: STATUS.md@08042b0:340 ('nothing re-arms on its own'); F11 question, Research.md@08042b0:672

found_values.value: no switch action from the coprocessor: the ESC pack switches follow the enable node, through the latch, alone; the coprocessor's overcurrent and over-temperature action disarms the outputs. V288 (owner, 2026-10-01) has the ESC pack switch open within the 500 ms stop deadline after an over-temperature detection; with no coprocessor input on the switch drivers, the tree states no path for that, reported for P5
found_values.source: R3 row, Research.md@08042b0:310 ('R3's gates follow the enable node alone'); IOBoard.md@08042b0:227; Monostable.md@23c82ca:453-455 ('it cannot remove the enable or add to it'); V288 Answer, Research.md@08042b0:985

At 6.35 A: 8.9 mV and 56 mW a rail at 25 degC (derived). The BTS7004-1EPP fails it: VS(OP) 4.1 V. The 2N7002BK,215 of round 1 drove a P-channel switch, which cannot conduct at 0.8 V; it drops out

The controlled turn-off of round 1 stays refuted. A fast turn-off passes the device SOA with no sharing assumed: IPT015N10N5 1188 A at 85 V on the 1 us line (TC 25 degC), 594 A at TC 100 degC, 353 A at 2 us; IPT015N10NF2S 1139 A, 570 A, 351 A. It holds only with the pack node clamped (45 mJ in 1 uH at 300 A) and a freewheel diode on the switched node (22.5 mJ in 0.5 uH). report.value: No part qualifies. A capacitive clamp meets the switching transient: simulated (ideal 67.2 V pack, 1 uH, 10 uF ceramic, a bulk bank; derived), 300 A cut fast peaks under 82 V with 6 x 330 uF at 35 to 52 mOhm total series resistance or 8 x 330 uF at 30 to 52 mOhm (C +/-20 %), and the plug-in ring stays under 82 V only inside that window; 600 A needs about 3300 to 4700 uF at 20 to 30 mOhm. With little series resistance the plug-in ring reaches 117 V to 120 V. The only stocked 100 V part of an allowed maker, EEV-FK2A331M (JLCPCB 350), bounds its ESR from above only. A damping resistor (about 6 J a plug-in) or a pack connector that limits plug-in current (stage 2) closes it. Owner trade-off: a capacitive clamp with damping or a pre-charging connector, or the motor monitor moved off the pack node
report.source: [D39]; vendors.py jlcpcb C178734 (21:47:29Z); [D1], section 6.1; derived (scratch sim.py and win.py)

report.value: No module qualifies. data.ruling: The refutation holds. The requirement list for the Link CAN controller leaves out two requirements. The first is V16, the frames the panel sends during one flash stall, with its IOBoard.md row "Received frames held through a flash stall". The second is V26, the link controller clock's largest frequency error, with its IOBoard.md row "Clock accuracy". The Raised by P1 table assigns both questions to "R2, Link CAN controller". Both are answered "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)", which is the same status as V28, and V28 is in the list. The R2 category row requires R2 to report each controller's received frames against that send count and to state each controller's clock tolerance. The P4 row makes the datasheet verifier re-read the frames each R2 controller holds, each R2 controller's clock tolerance and each value found for research. Round 2's stage 1 rule keeps V26 open as a value answered for research, so the requirement still applies. The list entry "takes the 40 MHz clock" gives only the owner's frequency, with no error limit. The defect is in this function's requirement list, not in the part. The MCP2518FD datasheet text shows a FIFO up to 32 messages deep and FOSC1,40M at 40 MHz +/-0.5 %. Scope is function.

R2 states each controller's clock tolerance". data.ruling:
The refutation does not stand. It is true that the list leaves out V17 and V27, but neither omission makes the list wrong, and every entry it does carry was confirmed.

(1) V17 is not a requirement of this function. Its Research.md row says "(feeds Q8 only)". Under the P1 row, a value that only feeds a decision does not gate P2. Q8 is decided: an I2C FRAM, MB85RC256VPNF-G-AMERE2 (owner, 2026-09-29). So no frames-held minimum gates this controller. Round 1's list says the same: "no minimum gates the part". Frames held is a figure the category reports, not a requirement of the function. Its absence from the requirement list does not refute the list.

(2) V27 binds the clock that feeds the controller, not the controller itself. The Round 2 Follow-ups row puts the requirement on the clock function: "The 40 MHz clock of each MCP2518FDT-E/SL: a crystal or an oscillator, and its frequency error against V26 and V27". Where Round 2 and a category row differ, the Round 2 section holds. The verifier itself reports that the clock function carries the tolerance. On the controller side, the requirement is that the controller accepts the clock. DS20006027B Table 7-3 accepts a 40 MHz crystal or resonator within 40 MHz plus or minus 0.5 % (plus or minus 5,000 ppm). That band is wider than V27's plus or minus 3,876 ppm, so the omission hides no failure. The verifier also concedes that the part meets the clock figure.

What remains is a completeness note, not a refutation: round 1's list for this function carried both values. The category return should still state the frames each controller holds and each controller's clock tolerance, as the R2 and P4 rows ask.

figures.evidence: Set at power-up is what the tree holds: STATUS.md:340 'Every stop latches; nothing re-arms on its own', F11 answer (hardware latch, operator clear), IOBoard.md:224 and :226 (enable node low through the ramp; latch holds the enable low past the first edge). The 74LVC1G175 Table 4 reset row (MR L gives Q L) realises it with MR on the enable node.

Test step 7 (:557-561, 155 ms to 185 ms measured at the enable node) and step 10 (:582-585, band under retriggering) read the enable node, so the latch sits between the node and the gates; IOBoard.md:226 says the same. The gates named (buffer enable, servo rail gates, both ESC pack drivers, CAN standby) match IOBoard.md:218-227.

IOBoard.md:244 states a push button on the IO board, 434153017835, through an RC debounce and a Schmitt buffer to the latch clock; Monostable.md:449-455 puts no processor, register or firmware in the path; the WS-TASV datasheet shows a normally-open contact with 10 ms max bounce.

F11 asks a clear 'only by an operator action' (Research.md@08042b0:672); Monostable.md:449-455 and IOBoard.md:227 allow no processor, register or firmware in the path from GPIO6 to a gate: relay no, firmware no follows.

IOBoard.md:218 and :248 (owner, 2026-09-30): one high-side switch on each of the 3 servo rails and one on the adjustable output, 4 a board; the 20 port switches behind the I/O expander are not a gate; Monostable.md:449-455 keeps a gate off the expander.

INA228 absolute maximum VCM and VVBUS -0.3 V to 85 V (section 6.1, read 23:32:14Z); F15 gives 67.2 V; 85 - 67.2 = 17.8 V; a 100 V part leaves 32.8 V, an 80 V part 12.8 V. The switched node can reach 86 V (clamp plus the freewheel diode), which a 100 V part covers.
V50 answer (owner, 2026-09-28): 'Peak: 300 A for 30 s at most'; 'and more' carries no figure.

Fig. 7 of the 74HC423 (Rev. 8.1) digitized at 600 dpi: K 0.4810 / 0.4780 / 0.4750 at 3.201 / 3.3 / 3.399 V (+/-0.63 %); Rev. 8.1 has no K-against-temperature graph or limit, so that term is not read. The curve is for CEXT 10 nF.
Table 6 II +/-0.1 uA at 25 degC (VCC 6.0 V), +/-1.0 uA at -40 to 85 degC, no separate timing-pin figure; 0.1 uA x 2^(25/10) = 0.566 uA at 50 degC.
V270 answer (owner, 2026-10-01): 0 to 50 degC ambient; 'The same range answers V38's question for the safety gate and the ESC pack switches'.
Savox page lists 'Quiescent Current (mA) 5' for the SH-0255MG+ (read 23:40:05Z); Monostable.md:411-416 sets 5 mA a rail as the placeholder, a small servo idling at 5 to 10 mA.
F15 answer (:676) is 16 cells, 67.2 V; V41 (:738) asks for 'none' when only switching transients are clamped; no source states a sustained overvoltage.

74HC423 Table 7 nRD input LOW pulse width: 100 ns (25 degC), 125 ns (-40 to 85 degC), 150 ns (-40 to 125 degC) at VCC 2.0 V, the lowest supply the table gives; 125 ns is the -40 to 85 degC value; no 3.3 V row.
TPS55285 (SLVSI72A): VOUT 0.8 V to 15 V; VOUT and SW2 absolute maximum 17 V; VVOUT_OVP_FB 110.5 % to 120 % of FB (115 % typ; 18 V at 15 V); VIN OVP 22 V to 23 V; IOBoard.md:355 DC input 12 V to 20 V.

programmer_screen.c:199-201 lists 'Regen braking ... Puts braking energy back into the pack'; no figure for the current is in the tree. The statement that the 150 A of F2 'bounds' it is an inference from the onboard rating, not a stated limit.

programmer_screen.c:139-141 and :202-204 'Low voltage cut', per cell, 28 to 38 (tenths of a volt), default 34; settings.c:39-41 pack_cells 1 to 14: a 1-cell pack with the cut at 2.8 V. The cut is where the ESC starts pulling power back; the pack may sag below it under load (not stated).
STATUS.md:340 and F11 support a level set that nothing re-arms; the 74LVC1G175 Table 4 reset row gives MR L, CP X, D X: Q L, so a level on MR wins over the clock (set dominant).

data.ruling: The refutation holds. The document key labels two datasheets with the wrong revision. [D9] reads "Nexperia 74LVC1G17 Rev. 15 (3 September 2024)". data.ruling:
The refutation holds. The re-rank drops SN74LVC1G14DCKR for failing sourcing rule 5 because "no alternate that passes rules 1 to 4 is named". Rule 5 passes when a pin-compatible alternate exists that passes rules 1 to 4 and works in the same circuit. Not having named one is not a failure of the part. The Nexperia 74LVC1G14GW,125 (LCSC C265125) is such an alternate.
- It passes rule 1: it has an LCSC number and JLCPCB places it.
- It passes rule 2: Nexperia is on the S1 list.
- It passes rule 3: it is in the jlcparts copy of 2026-09-14.
- It passes rule 4: JLCPCB stock is far above the gate of 50 for a need of 5 (5 boards x 1).
- Its pins match the DCK package (SC70-5) pin for pin, it has the same function, and no firmware is involved.
- It meets all four requirement values P2 set for this function: I_off on the input, positive-going threshold (VT+) below 3.15 V at 3.3 V, a supply of 3.201 to 3.399 V, and 0 to 50 degC ambient.
- Its datasheet also states unlimited input rise and fall times, so the input transition-rate limit that removed the 74LVC1G04 does not apply.
The function has two ranked parts, so the dropped part could take rank 3 with this alternate carrying rule 5. The re-rank allowed the same route for SN74LVC1G175DCKR through 74LVC1G175GW,125. The facts behind the drop are correct: the Texas Instruments Digi-Key rows read 0 and the only stocked row is UMW (4), which is not on S1. Scope is function, not part: what holds is the drop reason within this function, checked against this function's requirement values. Nothing about the part itself fails, so SN74LVC1G14DCKR fails no other function.
